issues.description: Implementation introduces a 7 wei base-fee floor (Wei.of(7L)) enforced via satisfiesFloorTxFee that has no counterpart in the EIP-1559 spec. Spec only requires max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas with base fee allowed to decay toward 0. Code rejects any transaction where gasPrice/maxFeePerGas < 7 (unless initial base fee was zero) even when base_fee_per_gas is 0-6 and transaction would otherwise be valid.
issues.potential_impact: Mempool divergence and potential consensus divergence if floor is used in block validation: valid low-fee transactions per spec are censored/rejected by Besu but accepted by spec-compliant clients. Chain with low/zero base fee would stall or split. Also breaks exact EIP-1559 fee dynamics.
issues.suggestion: Remove consensus-critical floor. If spam protection is desired, apply floor only as non-consensus txpool policy, not in block validation, and document deviation. Make baseFee calculation allow 0 as per spec formula.

issues.code_location: LondonFeeMarket constructor, baseFeeInitialValue, getInitialBasefee(), computeBaseFee() fork branch
issues.description: Spec fixes INITIAL_BASE_FEE = 1000000000 and requires expected_base_fee_per_gas = INITIAL_BASE_FEE on fork block. Implementation allows arbitrary override via Optional<Wei> baseFeePerGasOverride (baseFeePerGasOverride.orElse(DEFAULT_BASEFEE_INITIAL_VALUE)). If override != 1e9 is configured, fork-block base fee will not match spec.
issues.potential_impact: Consensus failure / chain split if node configured with non-spec initial base fee; different clients disagree on validity of London fork block header base_fee_per_gas.
issues.suggestion: Enforce constant Uint(1000000000) for mainnet London fork block as in execution-spec fork diff (expected_base_fee_per_gas = INITIAL_BASE_FEE). Restrict override to testing/genesis-only paths with explicit warning.

issues.code_location: LondonFeeMarket.computeBaseFee() - entire function; missing gas-limit and tx validation
issues.description: Spec validate_block requires gas-limit bounds (block.gas_used <= block.gas_limit, +/- parent_gas_limit//1024 change limit, block.gas_limit >= 5000) and base-fee correctness (assert expected_base_fee_per_gas == block.base_fee_per_gas) plus transaction checks (max_fee >= base_fee, max_fee >= max_priority_fee, max_fee/priority <2**256, priority_fee = min(max_priority, max_fee-base_fee), effective_gas_price, burn base fee). This file only computes base fee; it performs no check_gas_limit, no gas_used vs gas_limit check, no max_fee >= base_fee check, no priority capping, no burn logic. Correctness depends entirely on unseen callers (e.g., TransactionPriceCalculator).
issues.potential_impact: If callers omit any check, invalid blocks/transactions accepted: over-limit blocks, wrong base fee, underpaying max_fee, uncapped priority fee, or failure to burn base fee (miner gets base fee) - all consensus-critical and enabling fee theft or chain split.
issues.suggestion: Ensure callers enforce all spec asserts: check_gas_limit as in reference calculate_base_fee_per_gas, validate header base_fee equality, enforce max_fee >= base_fee, max_fee >= max_priority_fee, priority_fee = min(...), effective_gas_price = priority+base_fee, and burn base fee (miner only gets priority_fee*gas_used). Add integration tests linking computeBaseFee + validation.

summary: Core base-fee formula (target=limit//2, denominator 8, elasticity 2, equal/no-change, increase with max(...,1), decrease, fork-block initial value) matches spec. However implementation adds non-spec 7-wei floor and configurable initial base fee, and this file alone does not enforce gas-limit, fee-cap, priority-capping or burn rules, leaving consensus safety to external callers.
